proposals.title: Arrival item 40's `pattern` was already prohibited by section 27.0 D1, and the recorded reason for the prohibition is now wrong
proposals.defect: Section 27.0 D1, from section 27.10's measured follow-up of 2026-09-04, says: never use `pattern` in a strict json_schema; use enums, minItems/maxItems, maxLength. Item 40 added exactly a `pattern` to fact_ids.items. The rule's recorded symptom (HTTP 400) no longer holds - lanes C and D both measured the gateway accepting it and enforcing it as a decoding grammar - which is strictly worse than the 400 the rule anticipated: a 400 fails in under a second, a grammar spends about nine minutes and 32,000 completion tokens per repository and surfaces as a truncation that reads like a batch-size problem.
proposals.consequence: Lane C's proposed fix (append `.+` to the pattern, add maxItems) keeps a pattern in a strict json_schema and still allows an ID that names no fact, caught only afterwards by binding_errors. Lane D's proposed fix (pin fact_ids.items to an enum of the packet's own fact IDs) is what D1 prescribes and what unit_id in the same function already does; it makes an ID that names no fact impossible to emit.
proposals.recommendation: The enum, with maxItems beside it as defence in depth. If the pattern form is kept, restate D1 and the section 27.9 G2-W20 purpose line in the same commit to say why a pattern is now allowed.
proposals.reversal: Lane E proposes no edit of its own; this is a reading of a standing rule against a landed commit. Refuted by one measurement showing this gateway decodes a bounded pattern safely, in which case D1's sentence is what needs the edit.
